_about: Drawn 3D board for site/boardviz (docs/how-to-contribute.md, Add a board drawing). Millimeters from the board's bottom-left corner, x right, y up, rot in degrees counterclockwise. parts: the hand-placed parts, each with a type the part library knows; a part with an id can carry a label and text shown when tapped. headers: cols x rows at 2.54 mm. Parts a picture does not show are left out.
source: Positions read from the top-side bench photo tda4/img/tda4-top.jpg, scale set from the 2.54 mm pitch of the 40-pin expansion header (20 rows). The board outline (99 x 110 mm) is measured off that photo, not taken from a drawing; positions are good to about 2 mm. Connector counts from docs/arrivals/tda4.md (TI's SK-TDA4VM user's guide). Chips that the photo shows but no document names are drawn without a label. Parts the photo does not show are left out.

parts.label: Expansion header
parts.title: 40-pin expansion header
parts.text: The 40-pin header on the left edge, laid out like a Raspberry Pi header so Pi add-on boards plug on. Nothing was connected to it in our runs.

parts.label: M.2 slot
parts.title: M.2 key E slot
parts.text: A slot for a Wi-Fi and Bluetooth card. The kit has no radio of its own, and the slot was left empty in our runs.

parts.label: The chip
parts.title: TDA4VM under the heatsink
parts.text: Two Arm Cortex-A72 cores that run Linux, the C7x DSP with its matrix accelerator for neural networks, and six Cortex-R5F cores, under a black finned heatsink. There was no fan in our runs.

parts.label: DDR memory
parts.title: 4 GB LPDDR4
parts.text: The working memory the Linux system and the models run in.

parts.label: Ethernet
parts.title: Gigabit Ethernet
parts.text: One wired network port. Ethernet ran at about 940 Mbit/s each way in our tests.

parts.label: USB Type-A
parts.title: USB 3.1 Type-A host port
parts.text: A host port for a keyboard, a webcam or a storage stick.

parts.label: USB Type-A pair
parts.title: Two stacked USB 3.1 Type-A host ports
parts.text: Two more host ports in one housing. The kit has three Type-A host ports in all.

parts.label: Serial USB
parts.title: Micro-USB, serial console
parts.text: Plug a micro-B cable from your computer here for the serial console. It shows up as four serial ports; the console is the second one on a Mac.

parts.label: Power USB-C
parts.title: USB-C, power
parts.text: Power in. The kit needs a 20 V USB-C power-delivery supply and does not include one.

parts.label: Power-on reset
parts.title: SW2, power-on reset
parts.text: Resets the whole board, as if power had been removed and returned.

parts.label: Boot switches
parts.title: SW1, boot mode switches
parts.text: A bank of small switches that picks where the chip boots from. The kit boots Linux from the micro-SD card.

parts.label: Camera connector
parts.title: CSI-2 camera connector
parts.text: One of two camera connectors. No camera was attached in our runs.

parts.label: Power LED
parts.title: Power LED
parts.text: Red when the board has power.
